noise_assumptions.notes: Reported assumptions for design context only. The official Task B uses QFF2026-v2 unchanged.

design_rationale: Our PS-Q2 kernel circuit is a 6-qubit ZZ fidelity circuit whose RZZ entanglers (CX-RZ-CX) act on a logical ring (24 CX and depth 41 in total). The topology contains the physical 6-cycle, so the ring is placed with zero SWAPs at the same cost as all-to-all. A chord closes a triangle, and the textbook QFT-3 (Nielsen and Chuang, Box 5.1) needs exactly that: H with controlled-S and controlled-T gives interacting pairs (0,1), (0,2), (1,2), and the final SWAP acts on (0,2). With the triangle the official QFT-3 needs 9 two-qubit gates, depth 18, swap overhead 0 and noisy fidelity 0.668, versus 12 gates, depth 21, overhead 1 and 0.627 for the 2x3 grid, and 0.604 for the bare ring. A grid, ring, line or star has no triangle, so one QFT pair is never adjacent and routing adds a SWAP (3 CX). All links are two-way because the benchmark enforces direction and one-way links add reversal gates. The rx, ry, rz and cx native gates are the organizer's fully-noised basis, so every compiled gate carries QFF2026-v2 noise. The cost is 7 couplers (14 directed edges), one more than a bare ring.
